description:
## What

Implement `ZlintBridge::run_on_cert(cert_der: &[u8]) -> Result<HashMap<String, Verdict>, PerCertError>` plus the per-cert SHA-256 verdict cache that makes the ~700-Lint adapter in `pkix-policy-zlint` viable.

## Architecture

Per PKIX-jy95.1: callers will spin up one Lint impl per zlint check (~700 impls), and each Lint will invoke `run_on_cert` for its check. Without a cache, that triggers 700 subprocess invocations per cert. The bridge caches by SHA-256(cert_der) -> HashMap<check_id, Verdict> so per-cert subprocess cost is paid once.

Cache lives on the `ZlintBridge` handle. Thread-safe (`Mutex<...>` or equivalent). Per-handle scope; if the consumer wants cross-handle persistence they layer their own.

## Implementation notes

- Pipeline:
  1. Hash `cert_der` (SHA-256).
  2. Cache lookup. If hit, return cloned `HashMap`.
  3. Write `cert_der` to a temp file (`tempfile` crate or `std::env::temp_dir()` + uniquification). Cleanup on drop.
  4. Spawn `<zlint_path> -format der <tempfile>`. Apply `BridgeConfig::timeout`.
  5. Read stdout. zlint emits one JSON object: `{"<check_id>": {"result": "<verdict_string>"}, ...}`.
  6. Parse verdict strings: `NA` / `NE` -> `Verdict::NotApplicable`; `pass` -> `Pass`; `notice` -> `Notice`; `warn` -> `Warn`; `error` -> `Error`; `fatal` -> `Fatal`. Unknown -> `OutputParseError`.
  7. Populate cache, return cloned map.
- Per-cert error mapping: zlint exits non-zero with stderr like `error parsing certificate: ...` for `MalformedDer`. Bridge maps to `PerCertError::MalformedDer { detail }`. Anything else non-zero is `Other { detail }`.

## Surface

`impl ZlintBridge { pub fn run_on_cert(&self, cert_der: &[u8]) -> Result<HashMap<String, Verdict>, PerCertError>; }`

## Tests

- Integration test against real zlint binary using a PKITS cert (already in workspace under `pkix-path/tests/pkits/certs/`):
  - First call returns populated map with > 100 entries.
  - Second call with same `cert_der` returns identical map (cache hit; assert no subprocess overhead via timing or instrumented bridge).
  - Mutated `cert_der` (single byte flip in a non-signature region; or simply use a different PKITS cert) returns different map.
- Malformed input test: pass empty `cert_der` or garbage; assert `PerCertError::MalformedDer`.
- Verdict-mapping unit test: synthetic JSON line with each of NA/NE/pass/notice/warn/error/fatal.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `run_on_cert` implementation + cache layer
- [ ] Tests: positive integration, cache equivalence, mutated input, malformed input, verdict-mapping units
- [ ] cargo build / clippy --all-features -D warnings / fmt --check / doc --no-deps clean
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased citing PKIX-jy95.7.3

## Out of scope

- `run_on_certs` batch (PKIX-jy95.7.4 — depends on this for cache primitives)
- Persistent / cross-process cache (caller responsibility)
